title: aCaMEL/hybridclassification pipeline parameters
description: aCaMEL NextFlow DSL2 for classifying hybrids from SNP data

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

popmap.description: Tab-delimited population map: sample and population (sampling site), no header

speciesmap.description: Tab-delimited species map: sample and species, no header

combinations.description: Tab-delimited file of species pairs to test, one pair per line (no header)
combinations.help_text: Each line names two species from `--speciesmap`, separated by a tab. The pipeline runs ADMIXTURE, NewHybrids and (optionally) bgc once per pair.

site_coords.description: Tab-delimited sampling-site coordinates (population, latitude, longitude; no header)
site_coords.help_text: Population names must match `--popmap`. If given, the report maps hybrid classifications by site.

geo_data_config.description: JSON file listing vector layers (for example rivers) to draw on the report maps
geo_data_config.help_text: Each entry gives a layer `path` (relative to `--geo_data_dir`), a `z_order` and a `style`. Requires `--site_coords`.

geo_data_dir.description: Directory containing the layer files named in `--geo_data_config`

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

filtering_options.title: Filtering options
filtering_options.description: SNP and sample filters applied with SNPio to each species pair.

ind_cov.description: Maximum proportion of missing data allowed per sample

snp_cov.description: Maximum proportion of missing data allowed per SNP

pop_cov.description: Maximum proportion of missing data allowed per SNP within either species of a pair, and later within any group (P0, P1, admixed) before NewHybrids and bgc

min_species_samples.description: Stop with an error if fewer samples of either species of a pair remain after SNP and sample filtering
min_species_samples.help_text: Without this check, a pair whose second species is removed by the missing-data filters would be analysed as a single species: ADMIXTURE would split it into two groups and NewHybrids would call 'hybrids' between them.

thin_dist.description: Keep one SNP (chosen at random, from `--seed`) within each window of this many bp

admixture_options.title: ADMIXTURE options
admixture_options.description: ADMIXTURE (via AdmixPipe), used to find candidate hybrids.

maxk.description: Maximum K to run in ADMIXTURE (from K = 1)
maxk.help_text: Candidate hybrids are taken from K = 2, so the default runs only K = 1 and 2. Larger values add runs for model comparison in the report.

ancestry_threshold.description: Samples whose larger K = 2 ancestry proportion is below this are treated as candidate hybrids

newhybrids_options.title: NewHybrids options
newhybrids_options.description: Locus panel, hybrid simulations and NewHybrids classification.

panel_size.description: Number of loci (highest F<sub>ST</sub> between P0 and P1) used for NewHybrids

sample_size.description: Number of individuals simulated per hybrid class, per replicate

prob_threshold.description: Minimum NewHybrids posterior probability to assign a sample to a hybrid class

af_dist_min.description: Minimum allele frequency difference between P0 and P1 for loci used in triangle plots and genomic clines

outlier_alpha.description: p-value cutoff for flagging samples outside the simulated hybrid index and interspecific heterozygosity distribution as unclassified

genomic_cline_options.title: Genomic cline options
genomic_cline_options.description: Optional hybrid index and genomic cline estimation with bgchm.

run_bgc.description: Estimate hybrid indices and genomic clines with bgchm

bgc_burnin.description: Proportion of bgchm iterations discarded as warm-up

reproducibility_options.title: Reproducibility options
reproducibility_options.description: Random seed for the stochastic steps.

seed.description: Random seed for SNP thinning, ADMIXTURE, hybrid simulation, NewHybrids and bgchm
seed.help_text: Each ADMIXTURE run gets its own seed, drawn from this one. If not set, a seed is derived from the run's session ID: it differs between runs, is kept by `-resume`, is printed at startup, and is recorded in the report. Rerun with `--seed <value>` to reproduce a run. Multithreaded ADMIXTURE is not bit-for-bit deterministic; give ADMIXTUREPIPELINE one CPU for exact reproduction.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
